messages.subject: Tagging question
parts:
Hi all,

I'm trying to create a small corpus of English literature, mainly to explore the present tense paradigm (somewhat like Gries and Hilpert (2010)). I want to be able to bring up a list of all present tense verbs, then to be able to divide them into groups in R, such as irregular and regular, division by person and number, division by which verbs are inflected with -s and which are not.

The tagsets that I've been able to find, usually have something for -s inflection (VVZ or VBZ, vs. VV or VB0), but is that too general? The London-Lund tagset has things like VA+0 for base forms and VA+3 for -s inflection. Would this be the better way to go then? Will adding the plus sign enable me to separate my present tense verbs by person and number when I try to subgroup within R? I was thinking I could even take it a step further and code VA+1+Z for first singular present tense with -s inflection.

Any help would be great!


David

messages.author: 1c45d11729c1781e
messages.subject: RE: [CorpLing with R] Tagging question
parts: >> I want to be able to bring up a list of all present tense verbs

I assume you are envisioning automatic POS tagging?

 

If so, what you want is only approximately possible, since no tagger I know of can distinguish accurately between present tense and other forms homophonous with the present. That’s the point of the label “base form” – because this tag covers more than just non-3s indicative present tense, ie it covers imperative and subjunctive moods as well. Depending on the tagger, the infinitive may or may not be distinguished successfully.

 

If you take into account that you will also be getting these other forms, then the union of “base form” and “-s inflection” – however they are tagged by the program you are using - will produce the list you want.

 

best

 

Andrew.
